newsitem.title: CHINA: China gives details of foreign bank yuan business.
newsitem.headline: China gives details of foreign bank yuan business.

text.p: China said on Thursday it soon would allow a few foreign banks to conduct local currency business in Shanghai and unveiled details of its plans.
The official Xinhua news agency said that the chosen foreign banks would not be allowed to have local currency debts exceeding 35 percent of their foreign currency debts.
Commercial bankers said that appeared to mean that China would restrict the amount of business by placing a limit on the deposits a foreign bank could accept.
Under Chinese accounting practices, like international accounting practices, bank deposits are treated as debts.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Xinhua also said that the central bank has already distributed a set of temporary regulations for foreign banks conducting business in the local currency, the yuan.
Foreign banks are now restricted to business in foreign currency and have been eager to gain a share of the business for taking deposits and making loans in yuan.
Foreign banks would have to adopt the regulations that applied to Chinese financial institutions, Xinhua said.
It did not elaborate but that appeared to mean foreign banks would have to accept the same tax rate used for Chinese banks -- one of the key obstacles to implementing the policy change.
Foreign bank profits are currently taxed at a 15 percent rate while Chinese commercial banks are taxed at 33 percent and the main state banks at 55 percent.
The official news agency said that authorities were still reviewing the banks that might be selected.
It repeated previous official statements that the policy relaxation would apply to banks in Shanghai's Pudong district, an area that China's economic planners have been eager to promote.

The official Shanghai Star newspaper has already said that three banks -- Citicorp's Citibank unit, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and HSBC Corp's Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp -- would be given licences for local currency business.
